messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool: tenant-omega-pool GPU utilization >= 95% for 4m. severity=page. links: https://console.redwood/obs/pools/tenant-omega-pool
Maya Chen: ack. I'm on it. pulling metrics and queue depth now.
Liam O'Neill: pinging infra to see if there was a scheduled job for omega. @Network Eng any scheduled data prep windows?
Network Eng: nothing scheduled in the last 24h for that pool. saw a burst of large requests ~10:12 UTC from tenant-omega (traffic-levels table)
Maya Chen: rough numbers: 12k concurrent tokens/s, avg seq len 1200, p50 latency 320ms, queue backlog 78 requests. KV cache hit ~8% — looks like many cold contexts.
Priya Rao: customer on Dedicated (VPC) with reserved 40 GPUs; current usage shows 42 GPUs of equivalent consumption due to large model (redwood-llm-2x) single-tenant heaviness. autoscale config: min=40, max=60, burst disabled by default.
Support Liaison: I'm drafting a short customer note. ETA 15m. Do we need to propose immediate mitigations or ask for permission for temporary burst?
Maya Chen: immediate steps I want to run:
1) reduce tenant concurrency to 60% at the gateway for omega
2) enable token throttling per-request for very long sequences (>2000 tokens)
3) consider a controlled manual burst (spin up 8 spare GPUs) if queue doesn't drop in 10m
If anyone objects call it out now.
Liam O'Neill: fine with throttling/concurrency reductions. For manual burst we need approvals for reserved billing impacts. @Priya can you confirm customer contract allows short-term burst?
Priya Rao: contract: reserved 40 GPUs with burst allowed up to +20% with manual approval from account exec. They have an enterprise SLA but cost responsibility for burst is on customer unless we grant a 1-off credit. Can ask account exec but might take 20–30m.
Maya Chen: ok executing step 1 & 2 now.
Maya Chen: `/infractl dedicated set-tenant-rate --tenant tenant-omega --concurrency 60%`
Maya Chen: applied. gateway metrics show immediate drop in new inflight from 78 -> 45.
Maya Chen: applying token trim rule:
```
route: /v1/generate
if request.tokens > 2000 then reject with 413 and suggestion: reduce max_tokens or use chunked calls
```
Support Liaison: customer-eng is on a call with Omega engineering, they just said they kicked off a big backfill job by mistake and can cancel it within ~10m. they're asking NOT to burst unless necessary.
Maya Chen: good. we'll hold on burst for now. continue monitoring.
incident-bot: [UPDATE] queue backlog reduced to 22, GPU util dropped to 78% after rate-limiting (5m)
Liam O'Neill: still seeing a few long-running KV cache warmups - maybe due to many distinct conversation prefixes. any chance of enabling prefix caching for tenant? @Dedicated-Pool-Service
Dedicated-Pool-Service: prefix caching disabled for this tenant for privacy reasons historically, but we can enable a best-effort cache for identical prefixes with opt-in. needs product approval.
Priya Rao: product says we can enable ephemeral prefix caching for 1h only if customer confirms consent. Support Liaison — please confirm with Omega.
Support Liaison: Omega engineering confirmed they will accept ephemeral caching for this window. they asked we keep logs scrubbed.
Maya Chen: enabling ephemeral caching flag (scope=1h)
Maya Chen: `/infractl pools set-flag --pool tenant-omega-pool --name ephemeral_prefix_cache --value true --expires '3995008400'`
incident-bot: action logged by Maya Chen. audit id: a3f1-omega-cache
Maya Chen: after cache and throttles the backlog is 6, GPU util ~62%, p50 latency 250ms. good.
Customer-Eng: customer asked for timeline. can we provide ETA to restore to normal? also asked whether any user data left the VPC or was routed elsewhere.
Maya Chen: no cross-tenant routing. no data left customer VPC. ETA to steady state ~20m unless they re-started job. I'll propose 30m conservative to customer.
Support Liaison: message sent: "We've applied short-term rate limits and ephemeral caching which should stabilize throughput; no data left your VPC. We'll monitor for 30m and follow up with a post-incident note." :thumbsup:
PagerDuty: handoff reminder in 40m to next oncall (Liam) since Maya needs to step out in 35m.
Maya Chen: quick note for runbook when handing off:
- incident id: 2026-ops-omega-01
- actions taken: throttled concurrency, token trim rule, enabled ephemeral prefix cache
- metrics to watch: queue_depth, gpu_util, p50_latency, kv_cache_hit
- rollback steps: remove ephemeral cache flag, revert concurrency to customer configured value, re-enable request routing
Liam O'Neill: I'll take over if oncall handoff triggers. @Maya please push final state in 5m before you step out.
incident-bot: [NOTIFICATION] manual burst request pending approval. requested by Maya Chen. requires Account Exec approval. imputed cost: +8 GPUs for ~1h.
Maya Chen: I canceled the manual burst request — customer canceled their backfill. closing manual-burst flow.
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] alert dedup: dedicated-pool: tenant-omega-pool GPU util normalized to <70% sustained 6m. incident marked mitigated. follow-up required: RCA and contract review for burst allowances.
Support Liaison: customer acknowledged and appreciated the speedy mitigation. asked for RCA and a follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
Priya Rao: noted for billing: since they canceled the backfill no burst charges. if we had burst we would have charged per contract.
Maya Chen: summary for RCA: root cause — accidental backfill job from customer that triggered sustained high seq-length inference; mitigations — gateway concurrency cap, token-trim, ephemeral prefix cache; why it bubbled — low KV cache hit and autoscale min was at reserved capacity w/o burst enabled. action items: (1) add a pre-approved short burst option for select enterprise customers with SLAs (2) improve tenant-side quota alerts (3) add clear UI/CLI control for ephemeral caching opt-in/out.
Liam O'Neill: will pick up RCA doc and start draft. Maya — thanks for lead. I logged postmortem ticket: PM-6612
Maya Chen: handing off to Liam in 12m. leaving notes in the incident channel. ttyl.
Maya Chen: :wave:
Liam O'Neill: oncall takeover noted. monitoring now. final status: mitigated, monitoring to continue through next 60m and then close unless regression. :white_check_mark:"
